# CWE-250: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges — Detection in IaC Scripts

---

## Core Weaknesses to Detect

### 1. Overly Permissive Identity & Access Management (IAM) Policies

**Description:** Granting wildcard or administrative-level permissions to roles, users, or service principals beyond what is minimally required.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `effect: Allow` paired with `actions: "*"` | Full permission granted |
| `resources: "*"` | Access to all resources |
| `AdministratorAccess`, `FullAccess`, `PowerUser` | Broad admin-level policies attached |
| `policy_arn` referencing admin-level managed policies | Over-privileged role assignment |
| `inline_policy` with unrestricted actions | Excessive inline permissions |
| `NotAction`, `NotResource` | Inverted logic may grant unintended access |
| `condition` block absent on permissive statements | No contextual restriction on privileges |

---

### 2. Privileged Container Execution

**Description:** Containers configured to run with root-level or elevated OS privileges, expanding the blast radius of compromise.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `privileged: true` | Container has full host kernel access |
| `runAsUser: 0` | Explicitly running as root user |
| `runAsNonRoot: false` or absent | No enforcement of non-root execution |
| `allowPrivilegeEscalation: true` | Process can gain more privileges than parent |
| `USER` directive absent in container build definitions | Defaults to root at runtime |
| `securityContext` absent entirely | No security constraints defined |
| `readOnlyRootFilesystem: false` or absent | Writable root filesystem increases risk |

---

### 3. Excessive Linux Capabilities

**Description:** Adding Linux capabilities beyond what the workload needs, granting near-root or full kernel privileges.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `capabilities.add: ["ALL"]` | Grants every available capability |
| `capabilities.add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]` | Broad admin-level kernel operations |
| `capabilities.add: ["NET_ADMIN"]` | Unrestricted network configuration |
| `capabilities.add: ["SYS_PTRACE"]` | Can trace/debug any process |
| `capabilities.drop` absent | No explicit removal of default capabilities |
| `seccomp` profile absent or set to `Unconfined` | No syscall restriction |

---

### 4. Overly Permissive RBAC / Role Bindings

**Description:** Service accounts or identities bound to cluster-wide or overly broad roles, violating least privilege for orchestration workloads.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `roleRef.name: cluster-admin` | Grants full cluster control |
| `verbs: ["*"]` in role rules | All operations permitted |
| `resources: ["*"]` in role rules | All resource types accessible |
| `apiGroups: ["*"]` | Unrestricted API group access |
| `automountServiceAccountToken: true` (default) | Token unnecessarily exposed to workloads |
| `ClusterRoleBinding` used where `RoleBinding` suffices | Unnecessarily broad scope |
| `subjects` containing overly broad groups (e.g., `system:authenticated`) | All authenticated users gain elevated access |

---

### 5. Root or Elevated Privilege Execution in Automation / Provisioning

**Description:** Provisioning scripts and configuration management tasks executing privileged operations without scoping or dropping privileges.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `become: true` / `become: yes` with `become_user: root` | Escalation to root for entire task scope |
| `user_data` or `startup_script` containing `sudo` commands | Elevated execution during bootstrapping |
| `run_as` or `execute_as` set to privileged accounts | Elevated context for automation tasks |
| `shell` tasks without privilege dropping | Persistent elevated shell execution |
| `command` modules invoking admin-level binaries | Unnecessary privilege in automation steps |

---

### 6. Overly Permissive File and Resource Permissions

**Description:** IaC-managed files, directories, or secrets configured with excessive access permissions.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `mode: "0777"` or `mode: "0666"` | World-writable files |
| `owner: root` without `group` or `mode` restriction | Unrestricted root-owned resources |
| `file_permission` or `directory_permission` set to permissive values | Broad access beyond minimal need |
| `secret` or `configmap` mounted without `defaultMode` restriction | Sensitive data world-readable |
| `defaultMode: 0777` on volume mounts | Overly permissive secret/config exposure |

---

### 7. Host-Level Access and Namespace Sharing

**Description:** Workloads configured to share host-level namespaces, effectively granting privileged host access.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `hostPID: true` | Workload can see/interact with all host processes |
| `hostIPC: true` | Shared inter-process communication with host |
| `hostNetwork: true` | Workload uses host network stack directly |
| `hostPath` volume mounts to sensitive paths (e.g., `/`, `/etc`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) | Direct host filesystem or socket access |
| `shareProcessNamespace: true` | Cross-container process visibility |

---

### 8. Overly Permissive Service / Compute Identity

**Description:** Cloud compute instances or services assigned identities with excessive permissions attached at the infrastructure level.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `iam_instance_profile` referencing admin roles | EC2/VM instance with admin-level identity |
| `service_account` attached to broadly scoped roles | Workload identity with unnecessary access |
| `managed_identity` with contributor/owner scope | Full resource group or subscription access |
| `scopes` set to `cloud-platform` or equivalent full-access scope | Unrestricted API access from compute |
| `grant` of `roles/owner` or `roles/editor` at project/org level | Over-privileged access inheritance |

---

### 9. Database and Service Credential Privileges

**Description:** Services configured to connect to databases or APIs using admin or superuser credentials instead of scoped credentials.

| Keyword / Attribute / Field | Implication |
|---|---|
| `username: admin`, `username: root`, `username: sa` | Admin-level database user in service config |
| `master_username` used in application connection strings | Superuser credentials exposed to application layer |
| `db_privilege: ALL PRIVILEGES` | Full database access granted to application user |
| `grant_all` or equivalent | Unrestricted data access beyond application needs |

---

## Summary of High-Signal Keywords

```
privileged, runAsUser: 0, allowPrivilegeEscalation, capabilities.add: ALL,
SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, cluster-admin, actions: *, resources: *, effect: Allow,
AdministratorAccess, hostPID, hostIPC, hostNetwork, hostPath, become: true,
sudo, 0777, automountServiceAccountToken, securityContext absent,
runAsNonRoot: false, defaultMode: 0777, docker.sock, FullAccess, owner: root
```

---

## Key Detection Principle

> Any IaC configuration where a **role, process, container, or identity operates at a privilege level broader than what the specific task demands** is a candidate for CWE-250. The primary signal is the **absence of explicit least-privilege constraints** or the **presence of wildcard, admin-level, or root-equivalent identifiers** in permission-related fields.

package glitch

import data.glitch_lib

check_permissive_mode(value) {
    value.ir_type == "String"
    regex.match("^0?(?:777|666)$", value.value)
}

check_permissive_mode(value) {
    value.ir_type == "Integer"
    value.value == 777
}

check_permissive_mode(value) {
    value.ir_type == "Integer"
    value.value == 666
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
    parent := glitch_lib._gather_parent_unit_blocks[_]
    parent.path != ""
    attrs := glitch_lib.all_attributes(parent)
    attr := attrs[_]
    regex.match("(?i)^(privileged|allowprivilegeescalation|hostpid|hostipc|hostnetwork|shareprocessnamespace|automountserviceaccounttoken)$", attr.name)
    attr.value.ir_type == "Boolean"
    attr.value.value == true

    result := {
        "type": "sec_def_admin",
        "element": attr,
        "path": parent.path,
        "description": "Execution with unnecessary privileges - privileged or elevated host access enabled. (CWE-250)"
    }
}

Glitch_Analysis[result] {
